- **Illumination:** 62.6% — a bright waning gibbous Moon  
- **Sun–Moon separation:** 104° — far enough from the Sun for good contrast  
- **Clear sky:** strongly favorable  

Look toward **azimuth 259°**, roughly **west-southwest**, about **one-third of the way from the horizon to directly overhead**. Because the Sun is in the east-southeast, the Moon is on the opposite side of the sky, which helps.

In bright morning daylight it will look much paler than at night, but an ordinary observer who knows where to look should generally be able to see it unaided.
